Quick reference

WaterDrink 3 to 4 L per person a day.
Plain bleach 5 to 6%: 2 drops per litre, 4 if cloudy, wait 30 minutes.
Or boil for 1 minute. More
SirensCzechia: wavering tone 140 s: go inside, close windows, radio on.
Germany: 1 min rising and falling = warning; 1 min steady = all clear.
Austria: 3 min steady = warning; 1 min rising and falling = take shelter; 1 min steady = all clear.
Poland: 3 min wavering = alarm; 3 min steady = all clear.
Italy: IT-alert on phones. More
Someone hurtCall 155 (or 112).
Not breathing: 30 hard pushes mid chest, 2 breaths, repeat.
Bleeding: press hard 10 minutes, do not lift.
Burn: cool under running water 20 minutes.
Cold and confused: dry clothes, sleeping bag, warm sweet drink. More
PoisoningSwallowed chemicals, medicines, plants or mushrooms: poison centre 224 919 293, 24 hours. Unconscious or struggling to breathe: 155. More
Smell of gasNo switches, no flames. Windows open, everyone out. Call 1239 from outside. More
RadioČRo Radiožurnál 94.6 or 90.9 FM (Prague).
Walkie talkies: PMR channel 8.
Night long wave: Polskie Radio 225 kHz. More
Food safety, doors shutFridge 4 hours. Half full freezer 24 hours. Full freezer 48 hours. More

Now

The first hour of an outage

  • Note the time the power went off. Food safety is counted from here.
  • Check whether it is just your house: look at neighbours and street lights, then bezstavy.cz or call 800 850 860.
  • Turn on the battery radio: ČRo Radiožurnál 94.6 or 90.9 FM.
  • Keep fridge and freezer doors shut. Start the inverter and move the freezer plug to it.
  • Fill the bath, kettles and every container while water pressure lasts. Pumps can fail later.
  • Switch phones to low power mode. Charge from the battery, not the car.
  • Unplug TVs, computers and the router so the surge when power returns cannot damage them.
  • Close doors to unused rooms and draw curtains at dusk to hold heat.
  • Check on neighbours, especially older people living alone.

After 24 hours

  • Eat fridge food first, then freezer, then the store cupboard.
  • Run the freezer on the inverter in blocks if the battery is running low: 1 hour on, 2 hours off keeps it frozen.
  • Agree a daily routine: one cooked hot meal, water treatment, radio news on the hour.

What to do if...

One card per situation. In every case: radio on, check on family and neighbours, follow official instructions over anything here.

Power cut
  • Go to The first hour.
  • Freezer on the inverter, water containers filled, radio on.
Flood
  • Before: check whether your street is on the official flood maps (povodňové mapy).
  • Move documents, medicines and valuables upstairs.
  • Turn off electricity and gas before water reaches sockets.
  • Never walk or drive through moving water: 15 cm can knock you over, 30 cm can float a car.
  • Afterwards: treat all tap water as unsafe until told otherwise.
Chemical accident
  • Go indoors at once, close windows and doors.
  • Switch off ventilation and air conditioning.
  • Seal gaps under doors and around windows with wet towels or tape.
  • Go to an upper floor: most dangerous gases are heavier than air.
  • Radio on, wait for the all clear.
Nuclear incident
  • Go indoors and stay in the middle of the house or the cellar.
  • Close windows, switch off ventilation.
  • If you were outside: shower and change clothes, bag the old ones.
  • Take iodine tablets only when the authorities tell you to; they protect only the thyroid.
  • Expect to stay inside 1 to 2 days; follow the radio.
Storm
  • Bring in or tie down garden furniture and anything loose.
  • Stay out of woods and away from trees.
  • Unplug electronics; charge phones and power banks beforehand.
Heatwave
  • Shade windows during the day, ventilate at night.
  • Drink regularly; check older neighbours.
  • Never leave children or pets in a car.
  • Know the signs of heatstroke (see Life saving).
Evacuation order
  • Grab bags for everyone, pets in carriers.
  • Turn off appliances except fridge and freezer; close water and gas.
  • Put out any fire, lock up.
  • Make sure the neighbours know.
  • Name and address card in each child's pocket.
  • Go where the authorities direct you.
Boil water notice
  • Boil water 1 minute for drinking, cooking, brushing teeth and baby bottles.
  • Or use stored water, or 2 drops of bleach per litre.
  • Showering is usually fine; keep it out of mouths.
Card payments and internet down
  • Use cash in small notes.
  • Keep the car at least half full.
  • Paper list of phone numbers; offline maps on phones.
Disease outbreak
  • Stay home if ill; one carer per sick person.
  • Wash hands, FFP2 masks in shared spaces.
  • Keep 2 weeks of supplies to avoid shops.

Life saving first aid

Call 155 firstPut the phone on speaker and keep it next to you; the dispatcher will talk you through it. The Czech Záchranka app calls 155 with one press and sends your exact location. Install it on every family phone now.

Not breathing: CPR
  1. Safe to approach? Then shake the shoulders and shout.
  2. Open the airway: one hand on the forehead, two fingers lift the chin. Look, listen and feel for breathing for no more than 10 seconds. Gasping is not normal breathing.
  3. Call 155 on speaker. Send someone for a defibrillator (AED) if there is one nearby.
  4. 30 pushes in the centre of the chest: arms straight, shoulders over your hands, 5 to 6 cm deep, 100 to 120 a minute (the beat of "Stayin' Alive").
  5. 2 breaths if you are trained and willing, then 30 pushes again. If not, keep pushing without stopping; that alone saves lives.
  6. Keep going until help takes over or the person starts breathing normally. Swap with another adult every 2 minutes; it is exhausting.
ChildrenIf trained: 5 breaths first, then 30 pushes to 2 breaths, pushing one third of the chest depth with one hand (child) or two fingers (baby). If not trained, use the adult method. Doing something is always better than doing nothing.

Unconscious but breathing: recovery position
  1. Kneel beside them. Put the arm nearest you out at a right angle.
  2. Bring the far arm across the chest and hold the back of that hand against their near cheek.
  3. With your other hand, pull the far knee up, then roll them towards you onto their side.
  4. Tilt the head back so the airway stays open and the mouth points down. Check breathing until help arrives.

Choking
WhoWhat to do
Can cough or speakEncourage coughing. Do nothing else yet
Adult or child over 1 year, cannot breatheLean them forward. Up to 5 firm blows between the shoulder blades with the heel of your hand. Then up to 5 abdominal thrusts: stand behind, fist above the navel, pull sharply in and up. Repeat
Baby under 1 yearFace down along your forearm, head low: 5 back blows. Turn face up: 5 chest thrusts with two fingers. Never abdominal thrusts on a baby
Becomes unconsciousCall 155 and start CPR

Stroke and heart attack
SignsWhat to do
Stroke: FAST
Face drooping on one side
Arm weak, cannot lift both
Speech slurred or confused		Time: call 155 immediately and note the time symptoms started. Nothing to eat or drink
Heart attack
Crushing chest pain, spreading to arm, jaw or back; sweating, breathless, sick		Sit them down, call 155. An adult with no aspirin allergy can chew one 300 mg aspirin while waiting, unless a doctor has told them not to

Heavy bleeding

Press hard on the wound with a pad or cloth for 10 minutes without lifting, and call 155. If blood soaks through, add more on top. Full bandaging steps are in Scout skills.

Cold and heat
ProblemSignsWhat to do
HypothermiaShivering, clumsy, confused, then shivering stops (serious)Out of wind and wet, dry clothes, sleeping bag, warm sweet drinks. Warm the body core first. Call 155 if confused
FrostbiteWhite, hard, numb fingers, toes, ears, noseDo not rub. Rewarm in warm water around body temperature, only once there is no risk of refreezing. See a doctor
HeatstrokeHot, red or dry skin, confused, headache, may collapseCall 155. Shade, remove clothing, cool with water and fanning, cold packs in armpits and groin

Home and winter

Shut offs: find them now
Shut offUsually found
Water stopcock (hlavní uzávěr vody)Next to the water meter (vodoměr), in the cellar or in a meter pit in the garden
Gas valve (hlavní uzávěr plynu, HUP)In a box on the outside wall or boundary fence, on the yellow pipe
Electricity main breaker (hlavní jistič)In the meter box at the boundary; the house fuse board also has a main switch (hlavní vypínač)
  • Find all three this week. Label each with a tag and take a photo for every family phone.
  • Check the gas box key and any tool you need are kept next to it.
  • Show every adult and older child how to turn each one off.

Smell of gas
  1. Put out any flame. Do not switch anything on or off: no lights, doorbell, phone or plugs.
  2. Open windows and doors wide.
  3. Close the gas valve if you can reach it safely.
  4. Get everyone out and warn the neighbours.
  5. From outside, call the gas emergency line 1239 (24 hours). If anyone feels ill, call 155.

The warm room
  • Choose the smallest room on the sunny side, ideally one you can heat safely. Everyone lives and sleeps there.
  • Hang blankets over the door and windows at night; draw them back on sunny days to let the sun in.
  • A tent pitched inside the room traps body heat around sleeping people; it is noticeably warmer inside.
  • Rugs and blankets on the floor, hats on, layers of wool, hot water bottles from the stove.
  • A battery carbon monoxide alarm in the room whenever any flame or heater is used.

Heating without mains power
OptionNotes
Gas boiler on the batteryMost gas boilers stop in a power cut because the pump and controls need 60 to 150 W. An electrician can fit a plug so the boiler can run from the inverter. Check the boiler manual first; it needs pure sine power
Wood stove or fireplaceThe best backup if you have one. Keep a winter's dry wood under cover and have the chimney checked every year
Indoor rated gas heaterOnly a model sold for indoor use, with an oxygen depletion sensor. Window slightly open, CO alarm on, never while sleeping
Body heatOne room, one tent, everyone together. Costs nothing
Never indoorsBarbecues, charcoal, patio heaters, generators, or a gas oven left on for heat. Each kills through carbon monoxide.

Stop pipes freezing and bursting

If the house will stay below freezing for more than a day, drain the water system. A burst pipe causes more damage than most outages.

  1. Close the main water stopcock.
  2. Open the highest taps first, hot and cold, to let air in.
  3. Open every other tap, including outside ones.
  4. Open the drain valve at the lowest point, usually next to the stopcock, into a bucket.
  5. Flush the toilets and leave the cisterns empty.
  6. Switch off the electric water heater before draining it. Ask your heating installer now whether the central heating should be drained or protected with antifreeze if the boiler is off for days.

Prevention: insulate pipes in cold spaces, and in a cold snap leave cupboard doors under sinks open.

Grab bags, documents and every other checklist are in Kits.

Staying in touch

  • Out of area contact: one person outside the region everyone texts. Local lines jam first.
  • Text, don't call. Texts get through on a weak network; calls often don't.
  • Check in on the hour by text or walkie talkie; keep messages short to save battery.
  • Walkie talkies: PMR channel 8, agreed family code: ______.
  • No phones: everyone goes to meeting point 1, then 2. Leave a dated note on the door saying where you've gone.
  • Install the Záchranka app on every phone, and save the numbers on paper too.

Make the battery last
  • Low power mode on, screen brightness down, mobile data off except to check messages on the hour.
  • Flight mode when you only need maps or this guide; GPS still works.
  • Keep phones warm in an inside pocket: cold batteries drain fast.
  • One power bank per person, charged from the home battery or the car.

Children, pets and practice

Helping children cope
  • Tell them what is happening in simple, honest words, and what the family is doing about it.
  • Keep routines: meals, bedtime, a little schoolwork. Routine is calming.
  • Give each child a job: torch keeper, water checker, radio listener at the top of the hour.
  • Limit how much frightening news they hear.
  • Games with no power: cards, board games, I spy, story telling, drawing, Morse code with torches, knots practice.

The tortoise in a cold house
  • Without its heat lamp, a tortoise's room can get too cold quickly. Keep it in the warm room, in a box with a lid and air holes, insulated with towels or polystyrene.
  • A hot water bottle wrapped in a towel at one end gives warmth; it must be able to move away from it. Refill as it cools.
  • An outage is not the time for hibernation: unplanned cold, or temperatures swinging up and down, are dangerous. Ask your vet now how to handle a cold outage for your tortoise.
  • Keep a few days of its food in the store cupboard.

Practice: a lights out evening

Twice a year, switch off the main breaker for one evening (keep the freezer shut) and live from the plan.

  • Could everyone find a torch in the dark within a minute?
  • Did the inverter start and run the freezer?
  • Could you cook a hot meal and boil water?
  • Did the warm room stay warm enough?
  • Did everyone know the meeting points and walkie talkie channel?
  • What was missing? Add it to the Kits list.

Listen freely, transmit carefullyAnyone may listen to any frequency here. Transmitting on amateur, marine or aviation bands normally needs a licence; PMR446 needs none. In a genuine life threatening emergency, international radio rules allow any means to call for help.

Morse code

• is short (1 unit). ▬ is long (3 units). Gap inside a letter 1 unit, between letters 3, between words 7. Works with a torch, whistle, horn or tapping on a pipe.

Supplies

Food: 90 days, family of 4

Built on calories first. Need is about 7,800 kcal a day (two adults around 2,200 and 2,000, two children around 1,800 each). The list gives about 836,000 kcal, roughly 9,300 a day, a 19% buffer for cold weather, physical work and waste. Adjust the children's share to their real ages.

Dried yeast (sušené droždí)20 sachets
Baking powder (prášek do pečiva)20 sachets
Vinegar (ocet)2 L
Spices: paprika, pepper, garlic powder, curry, oregano1 large jar each
Tea, coffee, cocoaTo taste
Multivitamins and vitamin D, adults and children90 days each person
Manual can openers2 (one will break)
Mung beans for sprouting (mungo fazole)2 kg

How to store it
Storage rules
  • Cool, dark and dry. Heat is what shortens shelf life.
  • Write the date on everything and eat the oldest first. Buy only what you already eat, so rotation happens naturally.
  • Build it in stages: 2 weeks first, then 30 days, then 90.

A day's eating, example
MealWhat
BreakfastOats with milk powder, sugar or honey, dried fruit
LunchCrackers or flatbread with peanut butter or tinned fish, tinned fruit
DinnerRice or pasta with lentils or tinned meat, tinned vegetables, tomatoes, stock
SnackNuts, chocolate, a handful of sprouts

Fresh greens without a garden: sprouting

Stored food lacks fresh vitamins. Sprouting lentils or mung beans gives crunchy greens in 3 to 5 days, even in winter, using food you already hold.

  1. Soak 3 tablespoons of lentils or mung beans in water for 8 to 12 hours.
  2. Drain, rinse, and leave the jar tilted mouth down to drain.
  3. Rinse twice a day with treated water.
  4. Eat when the shoots are 1 to 2 cm long, within 2 days.

For growing your own food through the year, see Grow.

Preserving food and a 2 week menu

Methods at a glance
MethodGood forKeepsKey rule
DryingApples, plums, herbs, mushrooms you know, beans6 to 12 monthsDry until leathery or crisp, store airtight. Oven at 50 to 60 °C with the door ajar, or warm airy room
FermentingCabbage (sauerkraut), cucumbers, carrotsMonths, cool2% salt by weight, vegetables kept under the brine
Water bath jarsFruit, jam, tomatoes with added lemon juice, pickles in vinegar1 year or moreOnly acidic foods. See warning below
SaltingPork belly, fishWeeks to monthsFollow a tested recipe; keep cold
Cold storagePotatoes, roots, apples, onionsWinterSee Grow, Keeping the harvest

Sauerkraut
  1. Weigh the shredded cabbage. Add 20 g of salt per kg (2%), no more.
  2. Massage it with clean hands for 10 minutes until it releases liquid.
  3. Pack tightly into a clean jar, pressing down until the liquid rises over the cabbage.
  4. Keep it under the brine with a weight. Leave a gap at the top; loosely cover.
  5. Leave at room temperature (18 to 22 °C) for 1 to 4 weeks, tasting from week 1, then move somewhere cool.

Pale scum on top is normal: skim it. Pink, slimy or fuzzy coloured mould means throw it away.

Preserving jars in a water bath
  1. Wash jars and new lids in hot soapy water and keep them hot.
  2. Fill with hot fruit, jam or acidified tomatoes, leaving about 1 cm space at the top. Wipe the rims.
  3. Close the lids finger tight, stand the jars on a rack or folded cloth in the pot (never directly on the bottom).
  4. Cover with water at least 3 cm above the lids and boil for the time in your recipe, usually 10 to 20 minutes.
  5. Lift out and leave 24 hours. Lids should be pulled down and not spring back when pressed.
Botulism warningNever preserve vegetables, beans, meat, fish or soups this way. These low acid foods need a pressure canner, or the botulism toxin can grow in the sealed jar without any smell or sign. Tomatoes need 1 tablespoon of lemon juice per 500 ml jar. Throw away any jar with a bulging lid, spurting liquid or bad smell, unopened and without tasting.

Uses only the Food tab store list. Cook dinner once a day, using the haybox for rice, lentils and beans to save fuel.

DayBreakfastLunchDinner

  • Add a handful of sprouts every day from day 4 (see Food, Sprouting) for fresh vitamins.
  • Children: milk powder twice a day, and a daily multivitamin.
  • Days 15 to 90: repeat the cycle, swapping in rotated fresh food from the garden or store as you can.

Water: store, capture, purify

UsePer person per dayFamily of 4, per day
Drinking and cooking (minimum)3 to 4 L12 to 16 L
Basic hygiene addedabout 5 L moreabout 20 L more

1. Store: the first 2 weeks

4 people × 4 L × 14 days = 224 L of drinking water. Storing 90 days (about 1,450 L) is not realistic, so plan to capture and purify after the first fortnight.

Water already in your house
  • Hot water cylinder (bojler): switch off its power, close the cold inlet, drain from the bottom tap. Often 80 to 200 L.
  • Toilet cistern (the tank, not the bowl): usable after purifying.
  • Rotate stored water every 6 to 12 months.

2. Capture: rainwater

Rule of thumb: 1 mm of rain on 1 m² of roof gives 1 litre, minus about 20% losses. A 50 m² roof in a typical Prague month of about 40 mm gives about 1,600 L, several times what you need to drink.

3. Purify
MethodHowKills or removesWatch out
BoilRolling boil for 1 minuteBacteria, viruses, parasitesUses fuel; does not remove chemicals
Hollow fibre filter (0.1 micron)Pour or squeeze throughBacteria, parasitesNot viruses or chemicals; must not freeze once wet
Gravity filter (ceramic plus carbon)Fill top bucket, collect belowBacteria, parasites, taste, some chemicalsSlow; scrub candles when flow drops
Household bleach, plain, unscentedLabel must say sodium hypochlorite (chlornan sodný) 5 to 6%: 2 drops per litre, double if cloudy, wait 30 minutesBacteria, virusesNo fragrance or detergent. A faint chlorine smell should remain; if not, repeat and wait 15 minutes more
Chlorine dioxide tabletsAs per packBacteria, viruses, most parasitesSome parasites need up to 4 hours
Sunlight (SODIS)Clear PET bottle, 6 hours full sun, 2 days if cloudyBacteria, virusesClear water only; weak in Czech winter

Build a gravity filter

Parts, available in Czechia
PartCzech nameWhereNotes
2 food grade buckets with lids, 15 to 25 Lpotravinářský kbelík s víkemBeekeeping shops (honey buckets) (včelařské potřeby), KauflandCup and fork symbol, plastic type 2 (HDPE) or 5 (PP). Same size so they stack
2 ceramic filter candles with carbon corekeramická filtrační svíčkaDoulton EU store: British Berkefeld Ultra Sterasyl 8674, €30.95 each, wing nuts and washers included, free delivery over €25. Alternatives: search "Ultra Sterasyl" on eBay.de or Amazon.de, buying only from EU based sellersThe part that cleans the water; do not economise. Avoid unbranded copies with no test certificates
Plastic tapvýtokový kohoutKaufland: hünersdorff HD-PE tap, or a camping canister tapComes with nut and rubber washer
Step drill bitstupňovitý vrtákHornbach, OBIClean round holes without cracking the plastic
Food grade silicone (optional)potravinářský silikonHornbach, OBIFor a drip free tap

About 2,000 to 2,500 Kč in total; the two candles are about €62 of that.

Build steps
  1. Upper bucket: drill 2 holes in the bottom, about 10 cm apart, sized to the candle stems (check the box; usually about 13 mm).
  2. Lower bucket lid: stand the upper bucket on it, mark through the holes and drill matching holes so the stems drip straight through.
  3. Tap: drill a hole about 5 cm above the bottom of the lower bucket so sediment stays below the outlet. Fit the tap with the washer inside.
  4. Candles: soak in clean water for 15 minutes, then fit with a washer on each side of the plastic and the wing nut underneath. Hand tight only; ceramic cracks.
  5. Run it in: fill the top bucket twice and throw that water away to flush carbon dust out.

Using it
  • Pour in settled, cloth strained water. Mud clogs the candles fast.
  • Flow is slow, about 1 litre an hour per candle: fill it in the evening for the next day.
  • When it slows, scrub the candles gently with a clean scouring pad under running water.
  • Ceramic and carbon remove bacteria, parasites and bad taste, but not every virus. For rain, snow or stream water, add 2 drops of plain bleach per litre to the filtered water too.
Best combinationLet cloudy water settle, pour through a cloth, filter, then boil or chlorinate. Filter plus chemical covers both parasites and viruses.

4. Winter: storing water without burst containers

Water expands by about 9% when it freezes. Ice forms first at the top and sides, sealing the water underneath, so pressure builds until the container splits. Three ways round it: stop it freezing, leave room for the ice, or use the cold to your advantage.

MethodHowSurvives freezing?Notes
Store indoorsJerrycans under beds, in a cellar or inside cupboardNot neededBest option. Cool and dark, ideally 5 to 15 °C
Freezer fillerPlastic bottles 90% full in every freezer gapYesA full freezer stays frozen about twice as long in an outage
Room for the iceFood grade HDPE jerrycans or PET bottles about 85% full, cap a quarter turn looseUsuallyNever glass, never filled to the brim. Squat shapes cope better than tall narrow ones
Below the frost lineUnderground tank (podzemní nádrž), top about 80 to 100 cm deepNever freezesThe year round answer for rainwater; needs digging
Insulated box outsideContainer in a polystyrene lined box, on insulationDelays freezing by daysFor short cold snaps only. Bigger volumes freeze slower

Winterise the rain barrel

Before the first hard frost, usually in November near Prague:

  1. Close the downpipe diverter so rain goes to the drain.
  2. Empty the barrel, leave the tap open and store it upside down or indoors.
  3. Unscrew the cap on the first flush tube and leave it off until spring.

5. Snow as a water source

In a winter outage, snow is the water supply that keeps arriving. It is mostly air, so you need a lot of it.

Collecting it
  • Use only fresh, clean, white snow. Skip anything near roads, under trees, below roof edges, or where animals walk.
  • No frame? Lay the tarp on the lawn, or scoop the top 10 cm of a clean drift straight into the bucket.
  • Store collected snow outside in lidded buckets; it keeps as long as it stays frozen.

Melting it
Melting costs a lot of fuelMelting 1 litre of snow and boiling it takes about 0.2 kWh of heat, or around 0.5 kWh of gas on a camping stove. Melting all 16 litres a day this way would empty a 10 kg PB bottle in about 2 weeks.
  • Keep stored water for drinking; use snow for washing, cooking and flushing.
  • Melt with free heat where possible: a wood stove top, a bucket in the warm room overnight, or a dark container in sunshine.
  • Treat melted snow like rainwater: filter, then chlorinate rather than boil to save fuel.
  • Never eat snow as it is. It chills the body, and you spend energy warming it.

Car readiness

Keep in the car

Rules
  • Keep the tank at least half full, especially in winter. Petrol pumps need electricity.
  • The car can charge phones and power banks: run the engine 10 minutes at a time, outdoors only.
  • Never run the engine in a closed garage, even with the door open a little: carbon monoxide kills.
  • Stuck in snow: stay with the car, run the engine 10 minutes each hour for heat, and keep the exhaust pipe clear of snow.
Back to top

Power: solar and battery backup

Goal: keep a freezer running (about 100 W, with a short start surge of 600 to 1,000 W) and charge phones and laptops. A 24 V system with a 2.56 kWh battery and a 1,000 W inverter covers it.

Rules that matter
  • Measure the freezer first for 48 hours with the energy meter. That number sizes everything.
  • Panels in series: their combined open circuit voltage (Voc) must stay under 100 V, including cold mornings when it rises about 10%. Two ELERIX 450 W panels are fine.
  • Main fuse within 30 cm of the battery positive terminal. Every other device gets the fuse its manual names.
  • Connect the battery last, with the isolator off.
  • Keep the battery above 0 °C; LiFePO4 will not charge below freezing.
  • Never back feed the house wiring. That needs a changeover switch fitted by an electrician.
  • Keep it on the mains charger day to day so it is full when the outage starts. Winter solar is a top up.

Skills

DIY cooking without power

OptionIndoors?StrengthWeakness
Two burner stove on a 10 kg propane butane bottle (PB lahev)Ventilated onlyBest for 90 days. About 130 kWh of heat per 10 kg; bottles swapped at petrol stationsNeeds a regulator (regulátor tlaku) and hose
Butane cartridge stove (kartuše)Ventilated onlyCheap, compact, good first stoveWeak below about 0 °C
Alcohol can stoveVentilated onlySilent, cheap fuel (líh technický)Low heat, nearly invisible flame
Brick rocket stoveOutdoors onlyRuns on twigs and garden woodWeather, smoke
Haybox (retained heat)YesCuts fuel use by half or moreSlow; plan meals ahead

Cooking for 4 takes about 1.5 to 2 kWh of heat a day, so 135 to 180 kWh over 90 days: two 10 kg PB bottles, stretched further with a haybox.

Haybox (retained heat cooker)
  1. Bring the food to a full boil for 5 minutes, lid on.
  2. Move the pot straight into the nest and press the cushion on top. Work fast; every minute open loses heat.
  3. Leave it: rice 1 to 1.5 hours, lentils 2 hours, beans 4 hours or more.
  4. Bring back to the boil before serving if it has cooled.

Drinks can alcohol stove
  1. Cut the bottoms off two aluminium cans, about 3 cm tall each.
  2. Punch 16 to 20 pinholes round the rim of one, and a 2 cm hole in its centre.
  3. Press the halves together, holes up. Pour in about 30 ml of alcohol through the centre.
  4. Light, wait 30 seconds for the jets, then set the pot on the stand. Shield from wind with a foil ring.

Brick rocket stove (outdoors)

About 20 ordinary bricks, no mortar. Burns thumb thick sticks cleanly with little smoke, because air drawn under the shelf feeds a hot, tall flame.

Carbon monoxideEvery flame indoors makes carbon monoxide, which you cannot see or smell. Cook by an open window, never sleep with a burner on, and fit a battery CO alarm (detektor CO). Never use a barbecue, charcoal or rocket stove indoors.

Scout skills

Knots
KnotUseHow
Reef knotJoining two ropes of the same thickness, tying bandagesRight over left and under. Then left over right and under. Both ends of each rope must come out on the same side, or it is a weak granny knot. Never use it for climbing or loads.
Figure eightStopper so a rope cannot slide out of a hole or pulleyMake a loop, take the end round behind the standing part, then down through the loop. It looks like an 8.
Clove hitchTying a rope to a post, tree or tent poleWrap round the post, cross over the first turn, wrap again and tuck the end under the second turn. Pull both ends to tighten.
BowlineA loop that will not tighten or slip: rescue loop round the chest, mooringMake a small loop in the rope, end on top. "The rabbit comes out of the hole" (end up through the loop), "round the tree" (behind the standing part), "and back down the hole". Hold the loop and pull the standing part.
Taut line hitchAdjustable tension on a tarp or tent guy lineRound the peg, back to the line. Two turns round the line inside the loop, then one turn outside. Slide the knot to tighten.

Practise each knot until you can tie it in the dark. Five minutes a week with the children makes a good game.

Bandaging
  1. Heavy bleeding: press hard on the wound with a pad or clean cloth for 10 minutes without lifting. Call 155 or 112.
  2. Bandage the pad in place with firm turns, each covering about two thirds of the last.
  3. If blood soaks through, add another pad on top. Do not remove the first one.
  4. Check the fingers or toes: pink and warm is right; pale, cold or numb means loosen it.
  1. Support the injured arm across the chest, hand slightly higher than the elbow.
  2. Slide the triangular bandage under the arm, point towards the elbow.
  3. Bring the lower end up over the arm and tie it to the other end at the side of the neck, never on the spine.
  4. Fold or pin the point at the elbow so the arm cannot slip out.
ProblemFirst aid
BurnCool under running water for 20 minutes. Cover loosely with cling film. No butter, no ice
Tick (klíště)Grip close to the skin with a tick remover, pull straight out slowly, disinfect. Note the date; see a doctor if a red ring or fever follows
HypothermiaShivering, clumsiness, confusion. Get into dry clothes and a sleeping bag, warm sweet drinks, warm the chest first, not the hands and feet
SprainRest, cold pack wrapped in cloth for 20 minutes, firm bandage, raise the limb

Lighting a fire
  1. Clear a spot down to bare earth, ring it with stones, keep a bucket of water or sand next to it.
  2. Prepare everything first: two big handfuls of tinder, a bundle of pencil thin kindling, then thumb and wrist thick wood. Fires fail when you run out of the next size up.
  3. Light the tinder from the windward side, add kindling gently, then thicker wood once the flames are steady.
  4. Use standing dead wood, which is drier than wood lying on the ground. Split damp sticks to reach the dry core.
Tinder that worksIgnition
Birch bark (březová kůra), burns even when dampLighters, several, kept warm in a pocket
Cotton wool pads rubbed with Vaseline, stored in a tub (prepare now)Storm matches in a sealed tub
Dry grass, pine resin, wood shavings from a feather stickFerro rod: works wet, thousands of strikes
The lawIn the Czech Republic, open fires are not allowed in a forest or within 50 m of its edge, except at marked fireplaces. In dry periods regional fire bans apply everywhere.

Chemicals: what to use for what
NeedUseHowNever
Drinking waterPlain unscented bleach, 5 to 6% (chlornan sodný)2 drops per litre, 4 if cloudy, wait 30 minutesScented or "thick" bleach with detergents
Chlorine dioxide tabletsAs per pack; best all roundExpired tablets
Iodine tincture 2% (jodová tinktura)5 drops per litre, wait 30 minutesIn pregnancy, thyroid problems, or for more than a few weeks
Cleaning a woundLots of clean water or saline firstSaline: 1 level teaspoon of salt in 500 ml of boiled, cooled water
Disinfecting a woundOctenidine (e.g. Octenisept) or povidone iodine (e.g. Betadine)After rinsing, then a clean dressingBleach, strong alcohol or repeated hydrogen peroxide in open wounds: they damage tissue
HandsSoap and water, or alcohol gel of at least 60%20 seconds, every time after the toilet and before food
Surfaces, kitchenBleach 5%20 ml in 1 litre of cold water, mixed fresh each dayHot water: it breaks the bleach down
Vomit, faeces, bucket toiletBleach 5%100 ml in 1 litre of water, leave 10 minutes
Dehydration, diarrhoeaOral rehydration solutionSachets, or homemade: 6 level teaspoons sugar and half a level teaspoon salt in 1 litre clean waterToo much salt
Never mix bleach with anythingBleach with acid (toilet cleaner, descaler, vinegar) or with ammonia gives off toxic gas. Use one product at a time, with the window open. Bleach loses strength over 6 to 12 months, so date the bottle and replace it.

Other survival essentials

Heat
  • Pick one small room to live and sleep in; close the rest of the house.
  • Sleeping bags rated to at least minus 5 °C, one per person, plus wool layers and hats.
  • Hot water bottles filled from the stove.
  • No gas heater, barbecue or generator indoors.

Light
  • LED head torch for every person.
  • Rechargeable AA and AAA batteries, charged from the solar battery.
  • 2 lanterns, at least one solar or USB rechargeable.
  • Candles only in holders, never left alone.

Sanitation: bucket toilet

If water pressure fails, toilets stop flushing. A bucket toilet keeps the house hygienic.

  • Seal full bags and store outside in a lidded bin away from water sources.
  • Hand sanitiser by the bucket, used every time.
  • Toilet paper about 1 roll per person per week: 52 rolls for 90 days. Bin bags, heavy duty, 100.

Health
  • First aid kit: blister plasters, bandages, antiseptic, tweezers, thermometer.
  • Painkillers and fever reducers for adults and children, oral rehydration salts.
  • Ask your doctor about holding an extra supply of any regular prescriptions.

Tools
  • Battery or hand crank radio with FM, MW and DAB+.
  • Multi tool, duct tape, cable ties, rope, work gloves, tarpaulin.
  • Fire extinguisher and fire blanket near the cooking area.
  • Lighters and storm matches in a sealed tub. A whistle for each person.

Long term

Growing food near Prague

Climate factWhat it means
Last spring frost: usually late April, sometimes mid MayTender crops (tomatoes, beans, courgettes, pumpkins) go out after the "ice saints" (ledoví muži), 12 to 14 May
First autumn frost: usually OctoberHarvest tender crops before it; hardy crops carry on
Outdoor season: about 6 monthsIndoor sowing in March gives slow crops a head start
Winter lows often minus 10 °C, sometimes lowerOnly hardy crops survive outside; use a cold frame and indoor growing
Honest expectationsGrowing all of a family's calories takes several hundred square metres of potatoes and grains. A 20 to 30 m² vegetable plot will not replace stored food, but it gives fresh vitamins and variety from May to November, and stores for winter.

Outdoors: the raised bed
  • Raised beds warm up earlier in spring, drain well and save your back. 1.2 m wide lets you reach the middle from both sides.
  • Fill with layers: branches at the bottom, then turf upside down, then compost and good soil on top.
  • Full sun, at least 6 hours a day, near a water source such as the rain barrel.
  • Rotate each year: potatoes, then cabbages, then roots and onions, then beans and peas.

What to grow and when
CropSow indoorsSow or plant outsideHarvestNotes
Potatoes (brambory)NoMid AprilEarlies July, main crop SeptemberMost calories per square metre. About 3 to 4 kg per m²
Onions from sets (cibule sazečka)NoAprilAugustDry in the sun, store hanging
Garlic (česnek)NoOctoberJulyPlant cloves in autumn; winter cold is needed
Carrots (mrkev)NoApril to JuneJuly to OctoberStore in damp sand or a clamp
Beetroot (červená řepa)NoApril to JuneJuly to OctoberLeaves edible too
Peas (hrách)NoMarch to AprilJune to JulyTolerates light frost
Bush beans (keříčkové fazole)NoAfter 15 MayJuly to SeptemberLet some dry on the plant for winter

Tomatoes (rajčata)MarchAfter 15 MayJuly to SeptemberNeed the warmest, sunniest, sheltered spot
Courgettes (cukety)Late AprilAfter 15 MayJuly to SeptemberTwo plants feed a family
Pumpkin, Hokkaido (dýně hokkaido)Late AprilLate MaySeptember to OctoberStores 4 to 6 months indoors
Leeks (pórek)February to MarchMay to JuneOctober to MarchStays in the ground all winter
Kale (kadeřávek)NoMay to JuneOctober to FebruarySweeter after frost

Month by month
MonthJobs

FebruarySow leeks indoors; check stored vegetables

Stretching the season: cold frame

A cold frame adds about a month at each end of the season: salad and spinach from March, and fresh leaves into December. Build one from old windows on a wooden or brick box, back wall higher than the front, facing south.

Indoors in winter
GrowReady inHow
Sprouts: lentils, mung beans3 to 5 daysIn a jar, no light needed (see Food)
Microgreens: peas, radish, sunflower, cress7 to 14 daysShallow tray of compost, thick sowing, cut at 5 to 8 cm
Herbs: parsley, chives, basilOngoingPots on the brightest windowsill, south facing
Spring onions, lettuce stumps1 to 2 weeksRegrow root ends in a glass of water
Pea shoots2 to 3 weeksSoak dried peas, sow thickly, pick tips

A 20 to 30 W LED grow light for 12 hours a day uses about 0.3 kWh. In an outage, keep it off the backup battery unless the freezer is covered first.

Keeping the harvest through winter
CropStoreKeeps
PotatoesDark, frost free, 4 to 6 °C, in sacks or cratesUntil spring
Carrots, beetrootBox of damp sand in a cellar, or a clampUntil March
Onions, garlicDry, hanging, cool room6 to 9 months
PumpkinsIndoors, 10 to 15 °C, not touching4 to 6 months
CabbageFerment as sauerkraut (kysané zelí)Months
BeansDried, in jarsYears

Seeds
  • Keep a seed tin of the crops above, in a cool, dry, dark place. Most seeds last 2 to 4 years; onion and leek seed only 1 to 2.
  • Choose open pollinated varieties, not F1 hybrids, so you can save your own seed from beans, peas, tomatoes and pumpkins.
Back to top

Foraging

The one ruleEat nothing unless you are 100% sure what it is. Not 95%. If two features do not match, leave it. Drawings and photos help you learn, but check new plants with someone who knows them before you rely on them.
  • Try one new food at a time, a small amount, and wait a day.
  • Avoid roadsides, sprayed fields, and paths where dogs walk.
  • Wash low growing berries well or cook them: fox tapeworm eggs (echinokokóza) occur in Czech woods.
  • Czech forest law allows picking forest fruits for your own use, except in nature reserves and national park core zones.

Deadly lookalikes first
Lily of the valley (konvalinka vonná)
Convallaria majalis · more online

Photos: DenesFeri, CC BY-SA 4.0; Joanna Boisse, CC BY-SA 4.0. Wikimedia Commons.

Recognise by
Two broad leaves wrapped round one stem, white bells, no garlic smell
Autumn crocus (ocún jesenní)
Colchicum autumnale · more online

Photos: AnRo0002, CC0; Cillas, CC BY-SA 4.0; AnRo0002, CC0. Wikimedia Commons.

Recognise by
Leaves in a tuft straight from the ground with no stalks, appear in spring; pink flowers in autumn
Yew (tis červený)
Taxus baccata · more online

Photos: Mykola Swarnyk, CC BY-SA 3.0; Sdjurovic, CC BY-SA 4.0. Wikimedia Commons.

Recognise by
Short flat dark needles in two rows, red cup berries. Every part except the red flesh is deadly
Hemlock (bolehlav plamatý)
Conium maculatum · more online

Photos: Joanna Boisse, CC BY-SA 4.0; Famartin, CC BY-SA 4.0; Joanna Boisse, CC BY-SA 4.0. Wikimedia Commons.

Recognise by
Tall, white umbrella flowers, smooth stem with purple blotches, mousy smell
Water hemlock (rozpuk jízlivý)
Cicuta virosa · more online

Photos: AnRo0002, CC0; AnRo0002, CC0. Wikimedia Commons.

Recognise by
Umbrella flowers by water; hollow root with chambers. Among the most poisonous plants in Europe
Deadly nightshade (rulík zlomocný)
Atropa belladonna · more online

Photos: TB0815, CC BY 4.0; Robert Flogaus-Faust, CC BY 4.0. Wikimedia Commons.

Recognise by
Single shiny black cherry like berries sitting in a green star
Herb Paris (vraní oko čtyřlisté)
Paris quadrifolia · more online

Photos: unknown, CC BY-SA 2.0; Meneerke bloem, CC BY-SA 3.0. Wikimedia Commons.

Recognise by
One blue black berry on top of four leaves
Death cap (muchomůrka zelená)
Amanita phalloides · more online

Photos: Amanita_phalloides_1.JPG: Archenzo derivative work: Ak ccm (talk), CC BY-SA 3.0; Krzysztof Ślusarczyk (upload by Marek Ślusarczyk), CC BY 3.0; Krzysztof Ślusarczyk (upload by Marek Ślusarczyk), CC BY 3.0. Wikimedia Commons.

Recognise by
Greenish cap, white gills, skirt on the stem, sack like cup at the base. One cap can kill
Brown roll rim (čechratka podvinutá)
Paxillus involutus · more online

Photos: Gouwenaar, CC BY-SA 4.0; Lutz Blohm, CC BY-SA 2.0. Wikimedia Commons.

Recognise by
Brown cap with rolled edge, gills bruise brown. Once eaten in Czechia; can cause fatal immune reactions

Mushrooms
Do not learn mushrooms from a guideMost mushroom deaths in Czechia come from the death cap being mistaken for edible species. If you want to pick mushrooms, go out with an experienced picker first and have finds checked at a mushroom advice centre (houbařská poradna), run by Czech mycological societies in many towns.

Edible plants in Central Bohemian woods and fields
Stinging nettle (kopřiva dvoudomá)
Urtica dioica · more online

Photos: VerboseDreamer, CC BY-SA 3.0; VerboseDreamer, CC BY-SA 3.0. Wikimedia Commons.

Season
March to May
Recognise by
Square stem, stinging hairs, toothed leaves in opposite pairs
Lookalike
Dead nettles (hluchavka): no sting, also edible
Use
Young tops cooked like spinach or as tea. Wear gloves
Dandelion (smetánka lékařská)
Taraxacum officinale · more online

Photos: Famartin, CC BY-SA 4.0; Famartin, CC BY-SA 4.0. Wikimedia Commons.

Season
March to October
Recognise by
Leaves in a rosette with deep backward teeth, one yellow flower per hollow stalk, white milky sap
Lookalike
Cat's ear: hairy leaves, also edible
Use
Young leaves raw, flowers in batter, roots roasted
Wild garlic (česnek medvědí)
Allium ursinum · more online

Photos: Utente:Pervinca51, CC0; Guilhem Vellut from Annecy, France, CC BY 2.0; Derzno, CC BY-SA 4.0. Wikimedia Commons.

Season
March to May, damp shady woods
Recognise by
Strong garlic smell when crushed; each leaf on its own thin stalk; white star flowers
Lookalike
Deadly: lily of the valley, autumn crocus (see drawing)
Use
Raw or cooked. Pick one leaf at a time and smell each. Protected in some reserves
Raspberry (maliník)
Rubus idaeus · more online

Photos: AnRo0002, CC0; AnRo0002, CC0. Wikimedia Commons.

Season
July to August
Recognise by
Red berries that pull off as a hollow cap; leaves pale white underneath
Lookalike
None dangerous
Use
Raw. Leaves make tea
Blackberry (ostružiník)
Rubus fruticosus · more online

Photos: Acabashi, CC BY-SA 4.0; AnRo0002, CC0. Wikimedia Commons.

Season
August to September
Recognise by
Thorny arching stems; black berries with a solid core
Lookalike
None dangerous
Use
Raw or cooked
Bilberry (brusnice borůvka)
Vaccinium myrtillus · more online

Photos: ІваннаКеречанин, CC BY-SA 4.0; Michał J, CC BY-SA 4.0. Wikimedia Commons.

Season
July to August, conifer woods
Recognise by
Low shrub, green angular stems, dark blue berries with a crown, purple inside
Lookalike
Deadly nightshade grows taller with single shiny black berries in a star shaped cup
Use
Raw. Stains blue
Wild strawberry (jahodník obecný)
Fragaria vesca · more online

Photos: Michał, CC BY-SA 4.0; Ludwik Polak, CC BY-SA 4.0. Wikimedia Commons.

Season
June to July
Recognise by
Leaves in threes, white flowers with yellow centre, small red berries hanging down
Lookalike
Mock strawberry: yellow flowers, tasteless but harmless
Use
Raw
Rosehip (růže šípková)
Rosa canina · more online

Photos: T. Kebert, CC BY-SA 4.0; Filip Maljković from Pancevo, Serbia, CC BY-SA 2.0. Wikimedia Commons.

Season
September to November, best after frost
Recognise by
Red oval fruits on thorny rose bushes
Lookalike
None dangerous
Use
Tea or syrup, rich in vitamin C. Remove the hairy seeds, which irritate
Elder (bez černý)
Sambucus nigra · more online

Photos: Jonathan Billinger, CC BY-SA 2.0; S. Rae from Scotland, UK, CC BY 2.0. Wikimedia Commons.

Season
Flowers June, berries August to September
Recognise by
Woody shrub, flat white flower heads, black berries hanging down
Lookalike
Toxic: dwarf elder (bez chebdí): not woody, berries point upwards, smells unpleasant
Use
Flowers for cordial or tea. Berries cooked only, never raw or unripe
Hazelnut (líska obecná)
Corylus avellana · more online

Photos: Hladac, CC BY-SA 4.0. Wikimedia Commons.

Season
August to September
Recognise by
Nuts in leafy husks in clusters, round hairy leaves
Lookalike
None dangerous
Use
Raw or roasted
Lime blossom (lípa srdčitá)
Tilia cordata · more online

Photos: Ivar Leidus, CC BY-SA 4.0; Gmihail at Serbian Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 3.0 rs. Wikimedia Commons.

Season
June to July
Recognise by
Heart shaped leaves, scented cream flowers hanging from a pale leafy wing
Lookalike
None dangerous
Use
Dried flowers for tea
Ribwort plantain (jitrocel kopinatý)
Plantago lanceolata · more online

Photos: AnRo0002, CC0; AnRo0002, CC0. Wikimedia Commons.

Season
April to October
Recognise by
Narrow leaves with 3 to 5 parallel ribs, dark cone flower head on a long stalk
Lookalike
None dangerous
Use
Chewed leaf on stings and bites; young leaves edible
Pine needles (borovice lesní)
Pinus sylvestris · more online

Photos: George Chernilevsky, CC BY-SA 4.0; Emőke Dénes, CC BY-SA 4.0. Wikimedia Commons.

Season
All year
Recognise by
Needles in pairs, 4 to 7 cm, resin smell
Lookalike
Deadly: yew (see drawing)
Use
Tea from fresh needles, vitamin C. Not in pregnancy

The "photos" links need internet. Open each once while online and look at several photos per plant, in every season, alongside the drawings here.

Foraging calendar
MonthsWhat to look for
March to MayNettle tops, dandelion leaves, wild garlic
June to JulyElderflower, lime blossom, wild strawberries, bilberries, raspberries
August to SeptemberBlackberries, elderberries (cooked), hazelnuts
October to FebruaryRosehips, pine needle tea, dandelion roots
